cases.purpose: Under an EFAULT uname syscall, exercise the remaining individual selectors and a long selector: kernel fields fail per call while the -p/-i/-o constants still print as in GNU, preserving per-call status, empty command stdout, GNU diagnostics, shell continuation, and an unfiltered success control.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 uname(1) under the identical per-side seccomp ERRNO rule (pinned helpers/system-seccomp.py)
cases.comparison: Byte parity with GNU, including each diagnostic; bracketed stdout and stderr and per-invocation status expose partial output or failure to continue. The pinned seccomp helper and its setup control are shared with migration-uname-efault.

files.inner.sh:
mark() { printf '[%s]\n' "$1"; printf '[%s]\n' "$1" >&2; }
for args in -n -r -v -p -i -o --machine; do
  label="uname${args:+ $args}"
  mark "$label"
  uname $args
  printf '[%s] status=%d\n' "$label" "$?"
done
mark after
printf 'shell-continues\n'

cases.script:
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-seccomp.py
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" --errno uname:EFAULT -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc inner.sh
printf 'filtered-shell-status=%d\n' "$?"
uname -s
printf 'unfiltered status=%d\n' "$?"
cases.stdout:
[uname -n]
[uname -n] status=1
[uname -r]
[uname -r] status=1
[uname -v]
[uname -v] status=1
[uname -p]
unknown
[uname -p] status=0
[uname -i]
unknown
[uname -i] status=0
[uname -o]
GNU/Linux
[uname -o] status=0
[uname --machine]
[uname --machine] status=1
[after]
shell-continues
filtered-shell-status=0
Linux
unfiltered status=0
